market_wrap.text: Nifty rose 1.85% to 25,819 and the Sensex about 1,500 points as markets reopened after Tuesday's holiday and won back Monday's fall. Record foreign buying in November, Brent crude slipping to about $90 and a rupee at an eight-month high lifted banks, IT and FMCG (Nifty FMCG +3.8%); metals were the only sector to fall.

reasons.reason: Silver kept sliding: MCX silver futures were down about 2% in the afternoon, near ₹1.42 lakh/kg, on fears of a US Fed rate hike, a 19-month-high dollar and fund selling ahead of US PCE inflation data. The ETF fell further than the futures and closed near its 52-week low.
MCX gold fell about 1.3% to around ₹1.20 lakh per 10 g on the same Fed-hike and strong-dollar worries; Gold BeES touched ₹99.90 intraday and is down more than 13% so far in November.
No company news found today. Metals were the only sector to fall on a strong-rally day (Nifty Metal −2.0%), as a firm dollar weighed on metal prices, and BLEL slipped to a fresh 52-week low.

news.headline: US core PCE inflation 3.3% in October, above the 3.2% expected
news.summary: Headline PCE rose to 3.8%. The report makes a quarter-point Fed rate rise on 9 December look all but certain, a headwind for silver and gold.

events.detail: Meeting runs 2–4 December. The RBI raised rates in October; another rise would weigh on your bond fund and on small and mid caps.
Meeting runs 8–9 December; after hotter-than-expected October core inflation (25 Nov), markets fully price a quarter-point rise, the main pressure on silver and gold lately.
events.affects: Silver and gold funds (about 30% of the portfolio)

events.detail: Next reading of the Fed's preferred gauge, due after the December Fed meeting.
Companies usually report from mid-January to mid-February; results moved Manorama, Hindustan Copper and KRN this quarter.

outlook.view: Silver and gold fell again on 25 November (Silver BeES −5.5%, Gold BeES −2.9%) ahead of US inflation data. That data, out tonight, showed October core PCE inflation at 3.3% against 3.2% expected, cementing expectations of a December US rate rise, which has been the main pressure on bullion.
outlook.watch: The 8–9 December Fed decision and the dollar.

outlook.view: They have outperformed large caps this year, but lagged today's bank-led rally (Nifty Smallcap 100 −0.13%) and tend to fall harder when rates rise or foreign investors sell.
outlook.watch: RBI decision on 4 December and foreign investor flows.

outlook.view: A global sell-off in AI stocks hit Asian hardware names today (Taiwan −6.2%, Korea over 5%), weighing on AI-server maker Netweb, while Indian IT services stocks rose (Nifty IT +1.3%).
Record copper prices drove Hindustan Copper's profit surge, but copper has since slipped to a five-month low on a strong dollar and weak China data, dragging metal stocks.
outlook.watch: Global copper prices and the dollar.

outlook.view: The RBI is in a tightening phase, which tends to lower bond prices in the short term and raise yields on new bonds.
